instructions:
Model choice: list_workflows returns for each mode its license (open = free on the user's PC or a rented GPU, paid = billed per result by a provider and needs an API key), good_for (what it does best) and est_usd_per_result. When the user describes a task, recommend the best-fitting mode (e.g. text inside images -> a paid GPT Image mode, quick cheap photoreal images -> Nano Banana, long free clips -> open-source), state the price, and ask before using a paid one.
AI Video Studio For Windows generates AI video (open-source models: LTX-Video, Wan 2.2) on rented cloud GPUs (Vast.ai) from the user's own desktop app. The app must be running on the user's PC.
Money: a cloud card is billed the whole time it exists (starting, downloading models, idle, generating), not only while generating. The app closes its cards by itself after a few idle minutes. Use vast_running to show what is running and what it costs, card_start to prepare a card in advance, vast_stop (after asking) to close it at once, e.g. when the user says they are done.
Workflow:
1. Call video_studio_status first. If it fails, tell the user to open the "AI Video Studio For Windows" app.
2. Each video costs real money (about 0.05-0.50 USD, more for long clips on big GPUs). Before generate_video, tell the user the model, length and rough cost and get a clear yes. Only then pass user_confirmed=true. Batches: one confirmation for the whole batch is enough if the user approved the count and cost.
3. generate_video returns a job id at once; generation takes 1-15 minutes (cold start of a GPU is the slow part). Poll with get_job (wait_seconds up to 45) until status is done or failed. Do not start duplicate jobs while waiting.
4. When done, file_path is the .mp4 on the user's disk. Pass it to editing tools/skills. Report failures with the error text; make_report gives a diagnostic file.
Prompts: write English, cinematic, concrete (subject, action, camera, lighting, style). For several clips of one story keep the same style words and character description in each prompt. For image-to-video give image_path (a local file) and describe only the motion.
The user may name a model ("LTX", "Wan") and/or a GPU ("4090", "RTX 4090 24GB") in plain words. Pass them as workflow_id / gpu exactly as the user said; the app resolves them. If it replies that the GPU does not exist (e.g. "4090 Ti 16GB" is not offered), show the user the listed alternatives and ask which one; never swap silently. To change the app's permanent defaults ("use LTX with a 4090 from now on") call set_defaults. A per-video gpu/workflow_id overrides the defaults for that video only.
Models: ltxv-t2v / ltxv-i2v are fastest and cheapest; wan22-* are higher quality and slower. For pictures set kind="image" (FLUX or SDXL). Modes named fal-* and replicate-* run on hosted APIs (pay per result, no GPU, need the provider key); the others run on the user's PC (provider="local") or a rented Vast GPU (provider="vast"). The app's default place to run is shown by video_studio_status. Use list_workflows to see the options and their parameters.
More than video: list_workflows also has voice (kind tts: text to speech; vc: change a voice), picture tools (kind i2i: remove background, upscale, edit with words), smoother motion (v2v) and lip-sync (lipsync). Each entry lists its "inputs" (image/audio/video slots) and, for voices, its "languages": answer language questions from that list, never from memory. Chain steps with generate_video: set workflow_id to the tool and give "inputs" like {"image":"job:<id of the finished job>"} or {"audio":"C:\path\voice.wav"}. Typical chains: picture -> video (i2v), text -> voice (tts) -> lip-sync (video with a face + that voice), video -> v2v. Every step costs or takes time like a video, so confirm the whole plan once. For voice cloning, voice change and lip-sync on a real person, first make sure the user confirms the voice/face is their own or they have permission; do not help impersonate someone or make people appear to say things they did not say. Cloud cards: generate_video rents a card by itself (the GPU the user named, e.g. 4090) and installs the model on it. The FIRST video after a card is rented takes about 15-20 minutes (boot + download of about 38 GB of Wan 2.2); tell the user this and the price per hour (list_gpus) before starting. While the card stays up (it closes itself after about 10 idle minutes) each next video takes only 2-4 minutes, so for several videos send them all together. When the user says they are finished, ask and call vast_stop with all=true so billing stops. For "make me a video with Wan 2.2 from this picture" use workflow_id "wan22-i2v-lightning" with image_path; from text only use "wan22-t2v-lightning". To have a card ready before the first video use card_start with workflow_id and gpu.

tools.name: video_studio_status
tools.description: Check that AI Video Studio For Windows is running and configured (API keys present, output folder, active jobs). Call this first.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List available generation modes/models (id, kind t2v|i2v|flf2v, VRAM, typical seconds, adjustable parameters with defaults and limits).

tools.name: list_gpus
tools.description: Cloud GPUs currently offered with their USD per hour (min and median). Use it to estimate cost.

tools.name: generate_video
tools.description: Queue ONE video generation (costs real money). Ask the user for explicit confirmation including approximate cost first, then set user_confirmed=true. Returns a job id immediately; poll with get_job. Text-to-video by default; give image_path for image-to-video (and end_image_path for start->end frame).

user_confirmed.description: True only after the user explicitly agreed to the cost.

kind.description: image = still picture, audio = music, tts = speech, vc = voice change, i2i = picture tool, v2v = video tool, lipsync (default video).

provider.description: Where to run: the user's PC or a rented cloud GPU. Omit for the app default.

image_path.description: Local path of a start image (png/jpg) for image-to-video.

end_image_path.description: Local path of an end image (needs a flf2v workflow).

workflow_id.description: Model in the user's words ("ltx", "wan") or an id from list_workflows. Omit for the app's default.

gpu.description: GPU in the user's words ("4090", "RTX 3090 24GB"); omit for the app's default.

scene.description: Scene number; the file gets a sNN_ prefix (keeps story order).

inputs.description: Media inputs by slot key (see the workflow's inputs): value "job:<job id>" = result of an earlier job, or a local file path (png/jpg/webp, mp3/wav/flac/ogg/m4a, mp4/webm/mov).

extra_params.description: Other workflow parameters by key (see list_workflows).

tools.name: set_defaults
tools.description: Change the app's default model family and/or default GPU for all later videos (same as the settings in the app). model: free text like "ltx" or "wan". gpu: free text like "4090" or "RTX 4090 24GB"; "auto" lets Vast pick the cheapest. Without a Vast endpoint the choice is saved and applied later.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Status of a job. wait_seconds (max 45) waits until it finishes. status: queued|routing|generating|downloading|done|failed|cancelled. On done, file_path is the mp4.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: The 50 most recent jobs, newest first.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running job.

tools.name: retry_job
tools.description: Run a failed/cancelled job again (costs money again; ask first).

tools.name: card_start
tools.description: Start a cloud card on Vast NOW and prepare it (the models download), without making a video yet. Costs money while it runs. Ask the user first, then set user_confirmed=true. Returns at once; poll vast_running until the card status is running, then call generate_video. You do not need it before generate_video (that starts a card itself), only to have the card ready in advance.

workflow_id.description: Mode whose models the card needs, e.g. wan22-i2v-lightning (default: the last used one).

gpu.description: GPU as the user said it, e.g. 4090 (default: the saved choice).

tools.name: vast_running
tools.description: List the cloud cards currently rented on Vast (GPU, status, minutes running, cost so far, USD per hour). Every card listed is billed while it exists, even while loading. Call it when the user asks what is running or what they are being charged.

tools.name: vast_stop
tools.description: Close (destroy) a rented Vast card so billing stops: give id from vast_running, or all=true to close all of the app's cards. A job running on it will fail. Ask the user first, then set user_confirmed=true.

all.description: Close all of the app's cards (use instead of id).

tools.name: make_report
tools.description: Write a diagnostic report file (settings without secrets, recent jobs, log tail) and return its path. Use when something fails repeatedly.
